facts.statement: The genus Polycotylus includes the type species P. latipinnis and the species P. sopozkoi.
facts.quote: subdivision: * P. latipinnis Cope, 1869 P. sopozkoi Elphimov et al., 2016

facts.statement: Polycotylus lived in the Western Interior Seaway of North America near the end of the Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: It lived in the Western Interior Seaway of North America toward the end of the Cretaceous.

facts.statement: A fossil of an adult Polycotylus containing a large fetus provides evidence that the animal gave live birth, an unusual trait for reptiles.
facts.quote: One fossil preserves an adult with a single large fetus inside of it, indicating that Polycotylus gave live birth, an unusual adaptation among reptiles.

facts.statement: Edward Drinker Cope originally described Polycotylus based on fossils from the Niobrara Formation in Kansas in 1869.
facts.quote: Edward Drinker Cope named Polycotylus from the Niobrara Formation in Kansas in 1869.

facts.statement: A nearly complete skeleton of Polycotylus found in Alabama in 1949 was not formally described until 2002.
facts.quote: A nearly complete skeleton was found in 1949 from the Mooreville Chalk Formation in Alabama, but was not described until 2002.

facts.statement: The type species P. latipinnis was a medium-sized plesiosaur with a short neck, measuring between 4.7 and 5.4 meters in length and weighing over 1 metric ton.
facts.quote: It has a short neck and a long head, and was a medium-sized plesiosaur, with the type species (P. latipinnis) measuring 4.7 - 5.4 m long and weighing over 1 MT.

facts.statement: Researchers consider Polycotylus a basal polycotylid due to its higher number of neck vertebrae and a primitive humerus shape.
facts.quote: Polycotylus is thought to be a basal polycotylid because it has more vertebrae in its neck (a feature that links it with long-necked ancestors) and its humerus has a more primitive shape.

facts.statement: Distinctive features of Polycotylus include long pelvic ischia, thick striated teeth, a narrow pterygoid bone, and a low sagittal crest on the skull.
facts.quote: The long ischia of the pelvis are a distinguishing feature of Polycotylus, as are thick teeth with striations on their surfaces, a narrow pterygoid bone on the palate and a low sagittal crest on top of the skull.

facts.statement: Due to its short neck, Polycotylus was historically classified as a pliosaur within the superfamily Pliosauroidea, though it is closely related to true plesiosaurs.
facts.quote: Unlike some better-known long-necked plesiosaurs like Plesiosaurus and Elasmosaurus, Polycotylus had a short neck. This led to it being classified as a pliosaur, a marine reptile within the superfamily Pliosauroidea, closely related to true plesiosaurs (which belong to the superfamily Plesiosauroidea).

facts.statement: In 1997, phylogenetic analyses reassigned Polycotylus as a close relative of long-necked elasmosaurids.
facts.quote: In 1997, it and other polycotylids were reassigned as close relatives of long-necked elasmosaurids.

facts.statement: A 2007 study placed Polycotylus in the new subfamily Polycotylinae.
facts.quote: In 2007, Polycotylus was placed in a new subfamily of polycotylids called Polycotylinae.

facts.statement: Polycotylus lived in the seas of North America, Russia, and Australia during the late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Vivió en los mares de Norteamérica, Rusia y Australia hacia el final del Cretácico.

facts.statement: A more complete skeleton of Polycotylus found in Kansas was described in 1906.
facts.quote: Un esqueleto más completo fue hallado más tarde en Kansas y fue descrito en 1906.

facts.statement: The fossil LACM 129639, found in Kansas in the 1980s and described in 2011, contains an adult Polycotylus with a single fetus inside.
facts.quote: A fossil of P. latippinis catalogued LACM 129639 includes an adult individual with a single fetus inside it. LACM 129639 was found in Kansas during the 1980s and was in storage at the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County until it was described in 2011.

facts.statement: The fetus found inside the adult Polycotylus fossil was approximately 1.5 meters long, representing about 32 percent of the mother's length.
facts.quote: The length of the fetus is around 1.5 m, which is about 32 percent of the length of the mother.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence suggests that Polycotylus was viviparous, giving birth to live young rather than laying eggs.
facts.quote: This fossil suggests that Polycotylus was viviparous, giving live birth (as opposed to laying eggs).

facts.statement: Researchers believe the mother Polycotylus provided parental care to its single large offspring to ensure its survival.
facts.quote: Because it gave birth to a single large offspring, the mother Polycotylus probably gave it some form of parental care for it to survive.

facts.statement: Analysis of Polycotylus fetuses indicates that they sacrificed bone strength in the womb to achieve accelerated growth rates.
facts.quote: Examination of the fetus of Polycotylus indicates that while in the womb, plesiosaurs sacrificed fetal bone strength for accelerated growth rates.

facts.statement: Like other plesiosaurs, Polycotylus was a large marine reptile with a short tail, large flippers, and a broad body.
facts.quote: Como todos los plesiosaurios, Polycotylus fue un gran reptil marino con una cola corta, grandes aletas, y un cuerpo ancho.

facts.statement: Polycotylus had a short neck and an elongated head, reaching lengths of up to 5 meters.
facts.quote: Tenía un cuello corto y una cabeza alargada, midiendo hasta 5 metros de largo.

facts.statement: The genus Polycotylus includes several species such as P. latipinnis, P. ichthyospondylus, and P. tenius, along with several nomina dubia.
facts.quote: subdivision: P. latipinnis Cope, 1869 P. ichthyospondylus Seeley, 1869 P. tenius Hector, 1874 P. suprajurensis Sauvage, 1876 P. ischiadicus Williston, 1903 P. dolichops Williston, 1906 Nomina dubia: P. balticus Bogolubov, 1911 P. brevispondylus Bogolubov, 1911 P. epigurgitis Bogolubov, 1911 P. orientalis Bogolubov, 1911 P. ultimus Bogolubov, 1911 P. donicus Pravoslavev, 1915

facts.statement: It is debated whether viviparity was the most common reproductive strategy in plesiosaurs due to the difficulty of laying eggs on land.
facts.quote: Viviparity, or live birth, may have been the most common form of reproduction in plesiosaurs, as they would have had difficulty laying eggs on land.

facts.statement: Polycotylus is distinguished from other well-known plesiosaurs like Plesiosaurus and Elasmosaurus by having a short neck.
facts.quote: A diferencia de otros plesiosaurios mejor conocidos como Plesiosaurus y Elasmosaurus, Polycotylus tenía un cuello corto.

facts.statement: Polycotylus and other polycotylids superficially resemble pliosaurs like Liopleurodon and Peloneustes due to their short necks, large heads, and body proportions that differ from other plesiosaurs.
facts.quote: Polycotylus y los demás policotílidos se parecen superficialmente a los pliosaurios como Liopleurodon y Peloneustes debido a sus cuellos cortos, cabezas grandes, y otras proporciones corporales que difieren de los demás plesiosaurios.

facts.statement: In 1997, polycotylids were reassigned as close relatives of long-necked elasmosaurids.
facts.quote: En 1997, Los policotílidos fueron reasignados como parientes cercanos de los elasmosáuridos de cuello largo.

facts.statement: In a 2001 study, Polycotylus was classified as a derived cryptocleidoid plesiosaur closely related to Jurassic plesiosaurs like Cryptocleidus.
facts.quote: En un estudio de 2001, Polycotylus fue clasificado como un plesiosaurio criptocleidoideo derivado emparentado cercanamente con plesiosaurios del Jurásico como Cryptocleidus.

facts.statement: In 2007, Polycotylus was placed in a new subfamily of polycotylids named Polycotylinae.
facts.quote: En 2007, Polycotylus fue situado en una nueva subfamilia de policotílidos denominada Polycotylinae.

facts.statement: A recently described polycotylid named Eopolycotylus from Glen Canyon, Utah, was found to be the closest relative of Polycotylus.
facts.quote: Un policotílido descrito recientemente llamado Eopolycotylus de Glen Canyon, Utah, fue encontrado como el pariente más cercano de Polycotylus.

facts.statement: The genus Polycotylus was named by Cope in 1869.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Polycotylus (genus), Cope 1869

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Polycotylus is the subfamily Polycotylinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Polycotylinae

facts.statement: Polycotylus belongs to the family Polycotylidae.
facts.quote: Family: Polycotylidae

facts.statement: Polycotylus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Polycotylus lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Campanian stages, between 152.21 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Campanian (152.21 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: A fossil of P. latippinis cataloged as LACM 129639 includes an adult individual with a single fetus inside it.
facts.quote: Un fósil de P. latippinis catalogado como LACM 129639 incluye un individuo adulto con un feto único dentro del mismo.

facts.statement: The fossil LACM 129639 was found in Kansas in the 1980s and stored at the Los Angeles County Museum of Natural History until it was described in 2011.
facts.quote: LACM 129639 fue hallado en Kansas en la década de 1980 y fue almacenado en el Museo de Historia Natural del Condado de Los Ángeles hasta que fue descrito en 2011.

facts.statement: The length of the fetus is nearly 40 percent of the mother's length.
facts.quote: La longitud del feto es de cerca del 40 por ciento de la longitud de la madre.

facts.statement: Based on knowledge of fetal development in their relatives the nothosaurs, gestation was probably completed at two-thirds.
facts.quote: La gestación estaba probablemente completada en dos tercios basándose en lo que se sabe del desarrollo fetal de sus parientes los notosaurios.

facts.statement: This fossil suggests that Polycotylus was viviparous, giving birth to live young instead of laying eggs.
facts.quote: Este fósil sugiere que Polycotylus era vivíparo, dando a luz crías vivas (en vez de poner huevos).

facts.statement: LACM 129639 was the first direct evidence of viviparity in plesiosaurs.
facts.quote: LACM 129639 fue la primera evidencia directa de viviparimo en los plesiosaurios.

facts.statement: The lives of Polycotylus and other plesiosaurs followed a K-selection strategy, meaning few offspring were born per individual but each new offspring was cared for until maturity.
facts.quote: Las vidas de Polycotylus y otros plesiosaurios eran de Selección K, lo que significa que pocas crías nacían de cada individuo pero cada nueva cría era cuidada hasta alcanzar la madurez.

facts.statement: Because it gave birth to a single large offspring, the mother Polycotylus probably provided some form of care to ensure its survival.
facts.quote: Debido a que daba a luz una sola cría grande, la madre Polycotylus probablemente le daba alguna forma de cuidado para que sobreviviera.

facts.statement: F. Robin O'Keefe, one of the describers of LACM 129639, suggests that the social lives of plesiosaurs were "more similar to those of modern dolphins than to other reptiles."
facts.quote: F. Robin O'Keefe, uno de los descriptores de LACM 129639, sugiere que las vidas sociales de los plesiosauruios eran "más similares a las de los delfines modernos que a los demás reptiles."
